description: Write classes, WHERE-required, hidden writes, holds and their approval previews, and taint turning allowed writes into holds. Converted from the old engine's dangerous-statement, write-classes and approvals gate suites, plus v2 preview and taint cases.

cases.name: DROP TABLE on a read_write table is a schema change, refused by default
cases.sql: DROP TABLE webhooks
cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: DROP TABLE → deny dangerous_statement (regardless of read_write policy)

cases.sql: ALTER TABLE webhooks ADD COLUMN flag boolean
cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN → deny

cases.sql: ALTER TABLE webhooks RENAME TO hooks
cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: ALTER TABLE … RENAME (RenameStmt) → deny

cases.name: SELECT INTO is a table-creating write: a read-only policy denies the new table
cases.sql: SELECT id, email INTO _mp_leaked FROM users
cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: SELECT … INTO under default:read + block_ddl ON → denied (table_access catches the table-creating copy first)

cases.name: SELECT INTO on a read_write policy runs, with the new table's schema pinned
cases.sql: SELECT id INTO snapshot FROM users

expect.statement: SELECT id INTO public.snapshot FROM users

cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: SELECT … INTO on a read_write policy + block_ddl ON → allowed, same as CREATE TABLE AS

cases.name: CREATE TABLE AS is the same write as SELECT INTO
cases.sql: CREATE TABLE snapshot AS SELECT id FROM users

expect.statement: CREATE TABLE public.snapshot AS SELECT id FROM users

cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: SELECT … INTO on a read_write policy + block_ddl ON → allowed, same as CREATE TABLE AS

cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: block_ddl: false → DDL allowed by the guardrail (table_access permits)

cases.sql: DROP TABLE users
cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: block_ddl: false → DROP on a `read` table still denied by table_access

cases.sql: DELETE FROM webhooks
cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: DELETE with no WHERE → deny dangerous_statement

cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: UPDATE with no WHERE → deny

cases.sql: DELETE FROM webhooks WHERE id = 1
cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: DELETE WITH a WHERE → allow (guardrail is missing-WHERE only)

cases.sql: UPDATE webhooks SET enabled = true WHERE id = 1
cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: UPDATE WITH a WHERE → allow

cases.sql: DELETE FROM webhooks WHERE true
cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: DELETE WHERE true → allow (an explicit WHERE is not unqualified)

cases.name: a no-WHERE DELETE hidden in a CTE is a hidden write
cases.sql: WITH d AS (DELETE FROM webhooks RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM d
cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: no-WHERE DELETE hidden in a CTE → deny (fail-closed on nested DML)

cases.origin: engine/test/adversarial/dangerous-statement.test.ts: block_unqualified_dml: false → no-WHERE DELETE allowed

cases.name: preview: UPDATE ... WHERE counts the target rows the WHERE matches

preview.sql: SELECT pg_catalog.count(*) AS count FROM orders WHERE status = 'open' AND created_at < '2024-01-01'

cases.name: preview: the target's alias carries over
cases.sql: UPDATE orders AS o SET status = 'refunded' WHERE o.id = 1

preview.sql: SELECT pg_catalog.count(*) AS count FROM orders AS o WHERE o.id = 1

cases.name: preview: ONLY carries over

preview.sql: SELECT pg_catalog.count(*) AS count FROM ONLY orders WHERE id = 1

cases.name: preview: UPDATE ... FROM counts each target row once, through EXISTS
cases.sql: UPDATE orders SET status = 'refunded' FROM refunds r WHERE r.order_id = orders.id

preview.sql: SELECT pg_catalog.count(*) AS count FROM orders WHERE EXISTS (SELECT FROM refunds AS r WHERE r.order_id = orders.id)

cases.name: preview: UPDATE ... FROM with a target alias
cases.sql: UPDATE orders o SET status = 'refunded', total = o.total - r.amount FROM refunds r WHERE r.order_id = o.id AND r.amount > 0

preview.sql: SELECT pg_catalog.count(*) AS count FROM orders AS o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT FROM refunds AS r WHERE r.order_id = o.id AND r.amount > 0)

cases.name: preview: UPDATE ... FROM whose WHERE names only the target still needs a FROM row to change anything
cases.sql: UPDATE orders SET total = r.amount FROM refunds r WHERE orders.id = 5

preview.sql: SELECT pg_catalog.count(*) AS count FROM orders WHERE EXISTS (SELECT FROM refunds AS r WHERE orders.id = 5)

cases.name: preview: UPDATE ... FROM a join
cases.sql: UPDATE orders SET status = 'x' FROM refunds r JOIN users u ON u.id = r.order_id WHERE r.order_id = orders.id AND u.org_id = 7

preview.sql: SELECT pg_catalog.count(*) AS count FROM orders WHERE EXISTS (SELECT FROM refunds AS r JOIN users AS u ON u.id = r.order_id WHERE r.order_id = orders.id AND u.org_id = 7)

cases.name: preview: bulk UPDATE ... FROM VALUES
cases.sql: UPDATE orders SET status = v.status FROM (VALUES (1, 'shipped'), (2, 'refunded')) AS v(id, status) WHERE v.id = orders.id

preview.sql: SELECT pg_catalog.count(*) AS count FROM orders WHERE EXISTS (SELECT FROM ( VALUES (1, 'shipped'), (2, 'refunded') ) AS v(id, status) WHERE v.id = orders.id)
